title: Nodal and balanced preparation of a semistable Hilbert trait
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $g\geq2$, $d=20(g-1)$, $r=19(g-1)$, and $P(e)=de+1-g$. Let $Z=\operatorname{Hilb}^{P}(\mathbf P^{r-1}_k)$ and $J\subset Z$ be the projective Hilbert scheme and locally closed scheme of complete ten-canonical stable genus-$g$ embeddings of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability, lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter]. Choose $m$ at least the bounds in [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization, lem-sfb-gieseker-potential-stability] for these $g,d,r$, and equip $Z$ with the descended $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$-linearization $A_m$ of the former node. Let $R$ be a discrete valuation $k$-algebra with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and let $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z^{ss}(A_m)$ have generic restriction in $J$. Pull back the universal closed Hilbert family to $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_R$, and put $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$. Then $X/R$ is a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional geometric fibres having only ordinary nodes, in the unmarked convention of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]. In particular it has the relative dualizing line $\omega_{X/R}$ of that node. For an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of the residue field of $R$, put $C=X_\Omega$, $L_C=L|_C$, and $T=L\otimes\omega_{X/R}^{\otimes(-10)}$. The restriction $T|_{X_K}$ is trivial. The embedding of $C$ is complete, $h^0(C,L_C)=r$, $h^1(C,L_C)=0$, and every genus-zero normalized component of $C$ has at least two node branches; a smooth rational component meeting its complement in exactly two points has degree one for $L_C$. Moreover $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$, $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=\Omega$, and $\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic, def-pc-genus]. For every nonempty proper reduced union $Y$ of components of $C$, with $k_Y$ nodes between $Y$ and its complementary union, one has
$$\left|\deg_Y(T|_C)\right|=\left|\deg_Y L_C-10\deg_Y\omega_C\right|\leq k_Y/2.$$
Degrees are sums of line-bundle degrees on normalized components [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; $\omega_C=\omega_{X/R}|_C$.

source.place: Morrison Section 3.3 Proposition 10, printed p.16: preparation of the universal family over a DVR; Stacks Tag 0AY8, more-morphisms.tex lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, supplies connectedness after flatness and generic reducedness are checked. Arithmetic genus uses the fibre Hilbert polynomial. Agent expansion of these inputs.

proof.text: The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian: its only prime is $(0)$ and its only ideals are $(0)$ and $k$. Thus [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] applies over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with $E=\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ and its identity embedding, to the given $R$-point of $Z$. Its representing property gives the specified closed family $X\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_R$, flat and finitely presented over $R$, with geometric fibre coordinate Hilbert polynomial $P$. The closed embedding is exactly projectivity in [def-kun-projective]; [lem-pc-projective-proper] consequently gives properness. By [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter], the generic restriction in $J$ makes $X_K$ an unpointed stable curve. Unpacking [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], its geometric fibres are nonempty, connected, reduced and nodal of pure dimension one. In particular $X_K$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected. No smoothness or geometric integrality of $X_K$ is claimed.

source.place: Section 3.3 Proposition 10, first pullback paragraph; universal property and definition of stable curves

proof.text: The generic fibre is reduced: for an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $X_K$, extension to an algebraic closure $\overline K$ gives a reduced ring $A\otimes_K\overline K$ by step 1, and $A\to A\otimes_K\overline K$ is injective (extend a $K$-basis). Nilpotents of $A$ therefore vanish. The total scheme $X$ is reduced as well. Indeed, for $x$ over the closed point, [def-weil-flat-morphism] says that $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $R$. Tensoring the injection $R\hookrightarrow K$ with $B$, using the injectivity clause of [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], gives $B\hookrightarrow B\otimes_RK$. For an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, the latter ring is a localization of $A\otimes_RK$, the coordinate ring of the reduced open $U_K$ of $X_K$, so it is reduced. A nilpotent of $B$ therefore maps to zero and is zero. Stalks over the generic point are already reduced because $X_K$ is reduced. This checks reducedness on all stalks without assuming the as yet unproved reducedness of the special fibre.

source.place: Flatness definition; tensor the inclusion of a domain in its fraction field; elementary localization argument

proof.text: Every generic point $x$ of an irreducible component of $X$ lies over the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Otherwise the flat local map $R\to B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has maximal ideal contracting to $\mathfrak m_R$. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to $(0)\subset\mathfrak m_R$ and the maximal ideal of $B$. It gives a prime of $B$ contracting to $(0)$. But primes of $B$ correspond to generalizations of $x$; since $x$ is a generic point of a component, its maximal ideal is its only prime. Its contraction cannot be both $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_R\ne(0)$. This proves the required dominance of all components.

source.place: Tag 00HS, lemma-flat-going-down, applied to the local ring at a generic point

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $R$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal. Every nonzero prime ideal of a PID is maximal: its generator $p$ is irreducible, and any ideal $(a)$ containing $(p)$ has $a$ a divisor of $p$, hence is either $(p)$ or $R$. Thus the spectrum has exactly $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_R$, whose local rings are $K$ and $R$. The base is integral and normal. Indeed write an element of $K$ as $a/b$ with $(a,b)=R$, cancelling a generator of the original numerator-denominator ideal. A monic integral equation, multiplied by $b^n$, gives $b\mid a^n$. Modulo $b$, the image of $a$ is a unit by $(a,b)=R$, so this divisibility forces $R/(b)=0$ and $b$ is a unit. Hence $R$ is integrally closed; $K$ is a field and therefore integrally closed. Finally every ideal of $R$ has one generator, so $R$ is Noetherian and its spectrum is locally Noetherian as required later.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; elementary coprime-fraction proof of integral closedness of a PID

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected] to $X_K/K$: properness holds by its projective embedding, and geometric reducedness and connectedness were checked in step 1. Thus $H^0(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})=K$. Now [lem-trf-proper-normal-geometric-connectedness] applies to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$: properness is step 1, the base is normal integral by step 4, $X$ is reduced by step 2, and every component dominates by step 3. Its conclusion gives nonempty geometrically connected fibres, in particular connectedness of $C=X_\Omega$. This establishes connectedness before invoking potential stability, whose statement requires it.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal; varieties.tex Tag 0BUG clause (7) for generic global functions

proof.text: Fix either point $s$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and an algebraic closure $F$ of $\kappa(s)$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\alpha} Z^{ss}(A_m)$ gives the Hilbert point of $X_F$ by the base-change representing property in step 1. It is semistable for the same Hilbert linearization: [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization] gives agreement of the descended $\operatorname{PGL}_r$ and $\operatorname{SL}_r$ semistable loci and their compatibility with field extension. The fibre $X_F$ is connected by step 5 and has polynomial $P$ by step 1. The bound on $m$ in the potential-stability statement is independent of $F$, so the chosen $m$ works at both points. Since $g\ge2$, $d=20(g-1)>9(g-1)$ and $r=d+1-g$, all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-gieseker-potential-stability] hold, including its bound on $m$. Therefore each geometric fibre is reduced, purely one-dimensional and nodal. Applied to $C$, the same node gives completeness of the embedding, $h^0(C,L_C)=r$, $h^1(C,L_C)=0$, the lower bound of two node branches on every genus-zero normalized component, degree one on each smooth two-point rational component, and the subcurve inequality with coefficient $d/(2g-2)$. No assertion about disconnected semistable curves has been used.

source.place: Section 3.2 Definition 7 and Theorem 8; Section 3.3 equation (6)

proof.text: Steps 1, 4, 5 and 6 verify the entire unmarked-family hypothesis of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]: locally Noetherian base, projective flat finitely presented morphism, and nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one with only ordinary nodes. Take zero sections. That node constructs the relative dualizing invertible module $\omega_{X/R}$ and says its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. In particular its restrictions are $\omega_{X_K/K}$ and $\omega_C$. This application uses neither relative ampleness of the dualizing line nor positivity of its degree on every component.

source.place: Tag 0E6R, lemma-gorenstein-dualizing, as packaged by the cited unmarked nodal-family statement

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter], over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ the line $L|_{X_K}$ is locally on that base isomorphic to $\omega'^{\otimes10}$, where $\omega'$ is the relative dualizing line of that node, namely the module $H^{-1}(f^!\mathcal O)$ of [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] for $X_K/K$. A nonempty Zariski open subset of the spectrum of a field is the whole spectrum, so the isomorphism is global; any permitted line from the base is a one-dimensional $K$-vector space, trivial after choosing a nonzero vector. It remains to identify $\omega'$ with $\omega=\omega_{X/R}|_{X_K}$, which by step 7 is the line of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction] for $X_K/K$ with its nodal dualizing datum $\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] for the proper flat finitely presented reduced nodal $X_K/K$, also $\omega'$ is invertible with a datum $\alpha'$ of [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum]. In any regular affine curve presentation of an open $U$, the normalizations $e,e'$ give $\varphi_U=e'^{-1}e:\omega|_U\simeq\omega'|_U$ with $\varphi_U\alpha(dq(a))=\alpha'(dq(a))$ for every polynomial $a$; the $dq(x_i)$ generate $\Omega^1$, so $\varphi_U\alpha=\alpha'$. At a smooth point some Jacobian determinant with $a=x_j$ is a unit, so $\alpha'$ is an isomorphism on the smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. That locus contains every generic point of $X_K$: points over a generic point of a component of $X_{\overline K}$ have zero-dimensional local rings, unlike nodes. On overlaps $\varphi_V^{-1}\varphi_U$ is a unit $u$ with $u=1$ on this dense open, so $u=1$ since $X_K$ is reduced (step 1). The $\varphi_U$ glue to $\omega\simeq\omega'$. Tensoring by $\omega^{\otimes(-10)}$ gives $T|_{X_K}\simeq\mathcal O_{X_K}$. No trivialization over $R$ has been inferred.

source.place: Section 3.3 Definition 9 and Proposition 10, generic ten-canonical identification; reviewer: comparison of the Gorenstein dualizing line with the Jacobian-normalized adjunction line (Stacks moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality] to the closed flat finitely presented family of step 1. Its field-polynomial comparison gives $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C(e))=P(e)$ for every integer $e$, hence $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=P(0)=1-g$. By [lem-sc-global-functions], the proper connected reduced nonempty curve $C$ over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=\Omega$. The reducedness hypothesis of that statement is now available from step 6.

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric; varieties.tex Tags 08AC, 08AE for the Hilbert/Euler comparison and 0BUG for global functions

proof.text: The fibre $C$ is finitely presented over $\Omega$ by step 1, so its affine presentations have finitely many algebra generators and it is quasi-compact; hence it is of finite type. The spectrum of $\Omega$ is Noetherian as for $k$ in step 1, so $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its structure module is quasi-coherent (on each affine it is the module associated to the coordinate ring), and coherent: over each Noetherian affine coordinate ring it is free of rank one, and its submodules are finitely generated ideals. Its dimension is one by step 6. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] to the quasi-coherent structure module: $H^q(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$ for $q>1$. The definition [def-pc-euler-characteristic] therefore reduces the equality of step 9 to $1-g=1-\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, proving $\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g$. This is arithmetic genus; it does not assert that the possibly singular curve $C$ satisfies the smooth-curve hypotheses of [def-pc-genus].

On each normalized component of $C$, apply [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] to line bundles. Iterating gives $\deg(\omega^{\otimes10})=10\deg\omega$, and applying it to $\omega\otimes\omega^{-1}\simeq\mathcal O$ gives $\deg\omega^{-1}=-\deg\omega$, since $\deg\mathcal O=\chi(\mathcal O)-\chi(\mathcal O)=0$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Summing over the components in $Y$ yields $\deg_Y(T|_C)=\deg_YL_C-10\deg_Y\omega_C$. The normalized components are proper smooth connected curves by [lem-trf-reduced-curve-normalization-genus], applied to the proper reduced pure one-dimensional $C$ over $\Omega$; these are exactly the dimension and properness hypotheses needed for degree additivity. Finally $d/(2g-2)=20(g-1)/(2(g-1))=10$. Substituting this in the inequality already obtained in step 6 proves both the displayed equality of absolute values and the bound $k_Y/2$ for every nonempty proper reduced component union, including disconnected ones.
